newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds ease in line with Europe, eyes on U.S..
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds ease in line with Europe, eyes on U.S..

text.p: Irish government bonds eased in thin late trade on Thursday in line with other European markets as attention turned to the U.S. ahead of the release of key economic data on Friday, dealers said.
U.S. September producer prices and retail sales data are due for release at 1230 GMT.
The expectation is for a rise of 0.3 percent in producer prices in September and for a rise of 2.8 percent year-on-year. A rise of 0.2 percent in retail sales in September is forecast.
By 1530 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000 had eased 15p from Wednesday's close to 107.20 to yield 5.85 percent.
The eight percent bond due 2006 had eased 20p from the close to 108.15 to yield 6.72 percent.
"It was a good performance by the Irish market. We are finishing around 82 (basis points) over Germany in the 10-year area which is not bad at all," one dealer said.
"The five-year area in Ireland finished hardly off at all. Phenomenal considering weakness at European short-ends and in the UK," the dealer added.
Dealers said German bunds and U.S. Treasuries had both slumped after low jobless claims data, which sparked fresh inflation fears and talk of imminent U.S. rate hikes.
"While both Germany and the U.S. came off pretty hard after the data, Ireland didn't come off that much at all which is encouraging," the dealer said.
